# github_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Archive your GitHub repositories into the locker, or sync your forks with upstream.

## Synopsis

```
github_tool [options]
```

## Description

Lists the repositories owned by the GitHub user, public and private, optionally
narrowed with `--include_repos` or `--exclude_repos`, and then runs one action on
each.

`Archive` clones each repository with Git into a temporary directory, zips it, tests
the zip, and backs it up to the locker as
`<archive_base_dir>/<user>/<repo>/<repo>_<timestamp>.zip`. Each run adds a new
timestamped zip. With `--clean` the `.git` folder is left out, so the zip holds only
the working tree.

`Update` asks GitHub to merge the upstream changes into the default branch of each of
your forks (the merge-upstream API). Repositories that are not forks are skipped.

The username and access token come from `[UserData.GitHub] github_username` and
`github_access_token` in `~/JoyBox.ini` unless given on the command line.

## Options

### GitHub

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-a, --action <Archive\|Update>` | What to do with each repository: back it up as a zip, or merge upstream into a fork. Default: `Archive`. Allowed: `Archive`, `Update`. |
| `-u, --github_username <github_username>` | GitHub user whose repositories are used; `[UserData.GitHub] github_username` when omitted. |
| `-t, --github_access_token <github_access_token>` | GitHub personal access token; `[UserData.GitHub] github_access_token` when omitted. |

### Output

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-d, --archive_base_dir <archive_base_dir>` | Locker directory the archives go under, as `<dir>/<user>/<repo>/`; used by `Archive` only. Default: `~/Locker/Development/Archive`. |

### Selection

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --include_repos <include_repos>` | Comma-separated repository names to use, ignoring all others. |
| `-e, --exclude_repos <exclude_repos>` | Comma-separated repository names to leave out. |

### Archive

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-f, --force` | Not used by either action. |
| `-r, --recursive` | Clone submodules too (`git clone --recursive`). |
| `-c, --clean` | Leave the `.git` folder out of the zip. |
| `-l, --locker_type <locker_type>` | Locker to back the zips up to. Default: `All`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Archive every repository to all lockers

```bash
github_tool
```

### Archive two repositories with their submodules

```bash
github_tool -i "JoyBox,Dotfiles" -r
```

### Archive everything but one repository, without the git history, to the local locker

```bash
github_tool -e LargeRepo -c -l Local
```

### Sync all forks with their upstream

```bash
github_tool -a Update
```

### Preview an archive run

```bash
github_tool -p -v
```

## Notes

- The token needs access to private repositories for them to be listed, and write access for `Update`.
- Repository names in `--include_repos` and `--exclude_repos` must match exactly, including case.
- A repository that fails to archive or update is reported and the rest still run.
- For `Archive`, `--archive_base_dir` must already exist and Git must be installed with `setup_tools`.
